messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: P50/P99 divergence observed on streamly-prod-genapi

Folks —

Monitoring flagged a sudden divergence between P50 and P99 on streamly-prod's gen-api (us-west). Summary:
- P50 jumped from ~70ms to ~220ms over a 6m window.
- P99 increased from ~360ms to ~1.2s.
- Throughput stable but error rate clipped ~0.8% (mostly 429s at downstream fetch).

Top hypotheses: KV-cache churn + a small % of requests hitting fallback float kernels that are much slower (seen on a handful of hosts). I've attached a quick screenshot of the alert and heatmap (alert-screenshot.png).

Immediate asks:
- SRE/infra: can you triage hosts showing increased L3 miss / cache eviction traces? Marcus, can you confirm whether the recent kernel selection tweak rolled last night could explain this?
- Product: should we consider a temporary routing rule to route Streamly traffic to the compact/quantized model variant while we stabilize?
- CS/Account: we will likely need a short customer update within the hour. Suggest a calm, action-oriented note (I can draft).

I can jump on triage immediately.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Immediate: P50/P99 divergence observed on streamly-prod-genapi

Thanks Ben — good catch. A few quick directives so we move in parallel:

1) Triage first: Marcus / SRE team, please prioritize identifying whether the kernel selection change from last night (roll 20270706.kern) is responsible. If yes, snapshot those hosts and start a rollback canary ASAP.

2) Short-term mitigation: Product agrees to a temporary routing rule to the compact/quantized variant for Streamly only (route 25–50% initially). Marcus, can you confirm impact on latency on a 25% shift?

3) KV cache retention: engineering — increase retention knob for streamly-prod to keep prefixes warm while we investigate eviction patterns. If autoscaler behavior is evicting pods in a way that worsens cold starts, hold scale-in.

4) Customer note: I drafted a short update (customer-brief-draft.txt). Please review and flag any technical inaccuracies — I'll send once Marcus gives ETA for mitigation.

5) Escalation: If we expect SLA breach beyond 2 hours, we need an SLA exception approved from leadership. Evelyn, can you expedite that path if Marcus' ETA crosses 2 hours?

I'm on standby and can own the customer comms.

Subject: Re: Immediate: P50/P99 divergence observed on streamly-prod-genapi — triage notes

Quick triage summary (10:05):
- Root cause signal: a subset (~8%) of incoming requests had unusually high short-lived contexts (many tiny sessions, TTL < 30s). That pattern causes high KV cache churn which in turn drove a path to fall back to non-quantized float kernels on ~6 hosts that still had older kernel builds.
- We also see increased GCs on those hosts coincident with heavier CPU due to float kernels.

Actions taken (in progress):
- Isolated problematic hosts and removed them from LB rotation (draining).
- Forced model-routing rule: 35% of Streamly traffic -> compact-quantized model (rollout started 10:00).
- Disabled scale-in for the affected node pool for 45 minutes to prevent cold starts.
- Reverted kernel selection flag on a canary subset (two hosts) and running performance smoke tests now.

ETA & next steps:
- Expect measurable P99 improvement in 20–30 minutes if cache warming holds.
- If smoke tests confirm revert, will promote rollback across affected pool (30–45m).
- If rollback is blocked, next step is full routing shift to compact variant (cost impact noted).

Attachments: heap-dump.stf (collected from host-07), and I'm logging a ticket INF-3421 for follow-up (link below).

Links:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421
- Internal sandbox for smoke tests: https://staging.redwood.com/smoke/streamly

I'll post another update once smoke tests finish.

—Marcus

SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Streamly — brief update on performance and immediate mitigations

Alice —

Wanted to give you a concise update while our engineering team continues triage. We detected an increase in end-to-end tail latency for gen-api requests serving Streamly traffic this morning. We have taken the following actions to protect your traffic and restore normal latency: 

- Isolated and drained a small number of hosts showing elevated cache eviction and float kernel execution.
- Temporarily routed 35% of Streamly traffic to our compact/quantized model variant to reduce tail latency while we validate a kernel revert.
- Disabled scale-in on the affected node pool to avoid cold starts while caches warm.

What this means for you:
- You may see a transient improvement in p50/p99 within ~30 minutes; we will continue to monitor and follow up.
- We aim to avoid any functional change in responses — this is a performance routing change only.
- If you'd prefer, we can route a higher fraction of traffic to the compact variant temporarily; let us know.

We're tracking this as an operational priority and will share a full incident summary after remediation. If you want a brief call to walk through details, I'm available in the next hour.

Apologies for the interruption — we'll keep updates coming.

Best,
